text: A title card displays the text 'Introduction to Web Accessibility' over a gradient blue background with the Digital Bridge logo.
The instructor, a young woman in professional attire, stands before a projector screen showing the text 'Web Accessibility 101'.
An infographic appears on screen showing a world map with statistics: over one billion people with disabilities highlighted in yellow.
A slide displays the four WCAG principles as four colored pillars: Perceivable in blue, Operable in green, Understandable in orange, and Robust in purple.
The screen shows a side-by-side comparison: on the left, an image without alt text; on the right, the same image with a green check mark and descriptive alt text beneath it.
A video clip plays showing a student wearing headphones using a screen reader. Text output from the screen reader appears as an overlay at the bottom of the screen.
A code editor fills the screen showing HTML markup. Semantic elements like nav, main, and aside are highlighted in green, while generic div elements are highlighted in red.
Two text samples appear side by side: one with poor contrast showing light gray text on white, and another with strong contrast showing dark text on white with a green accessibility badge.
An animation demonstrates keyboard tab navigation. A visible blue focus ring moves sequentially through navigation links, a search field, and action buttons on a sample web page.
The Lighthouse accessibility audit results are displayed in Chrome DevTools, showing a score of 92 out of 100 with specific recommendations listed below.
The instructor gestures toward a slide showing the Digital Bridge logo alongside the ALX Savanna platform interface, with accessibility icons overlaid on the screen.
A summary slide appears with four key takeaways listed as bullet points, each accompanied by a relevant icon: a code bracket, an image, a keyboard, and a group of people.
